subject: Startups
title: Instagram's Simplicity Loop
description: A 60-second lesson on Instagram's Simplicity Loop.

hook.text: Instagram launched in 2010 and hit one million users in two months. No ads, no partnerships. Just a filter app.

buildup.text: The viral loop was sharing. Users took photos, applied filters, and cross-posted to Twitter and Facebook.

discovery.text: Every shared photo was an ad for Instagram. Friends saw beautiful images and wanted the same filters.

twist.text: Instagram deliberately kept features minimal. Fewer options meant faster sharing, which meant faster spreading.

climax.text: By making sharing the default action, Instagram turned every user into a recruiter without them even realizing it.

punchline.text: Simple products spread faster than complex ones.

quiz.question: How quickly did Instagram reach one million users?
